quest.title: The Wind Has Ceased
quest.description: There's an abandoned sanatorium on Windrest Peak...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x300, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

chapter.num: A Long Day in the Mountains: Prologue
chapter.title: Magic Mountain

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Well, well. If it isn't our great master of anti-self-termination, Josephus. So, why are you here, cursing all who live?

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Cut it out. Nobody dies in the Temple of Space.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: How strange. Did you try testing that rule, Sir Anti-Self-Termination?

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Keep talking, and a new batch of guards will be on its way.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Alright. Special times call for special treatment. I won't make fun of you.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Zeitlind. This is Josephus. He's a friend of mine.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: No need to be so sentimental. Everyone here is everyone else's friend.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: If you can't come to love or be loved by everyone over such long periods of time, you'd drown the world in sorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Come. Let us set our course for the heart of the world. A realm not reserved for the old or the dead, for the rich or poor.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Hehe, I've quoted that poem before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Maukie"... Paimon feels like she might've heard that before...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Ach. No, no. This isn't the time for that either.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Let me ask you, do any of you have combat strength on par with a junior Remurian Centurion or higher?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Don't worry, {NICKNAME} can beat people up just fine.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Come on, then. Let's head out and show them what Pankration, or maybe Machaira, means to you.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: It's safer here. I don't know why, but the suppression-type guards can't get in.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Organization-type Keepers usually don't harm people either. Unless you try to steal relics, that is.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, you've been gripping that suitcase this whole time. Your knuckles are all pale.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's safe here, so just put it down for now, 'kay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, unless you've got stolen relics in that suitcase. But that can't be, right?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Mhm.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, Paimon's sure it's gotta be full of valuable items.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Not really. Just some things I needed to say goodbye to before leaving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It's nothing.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You and your sister have vastly different personalities.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What did you say!?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Ah... I mean... Have you... met my sister? Did she come here before? So the "Hilda" you mentioned before really is...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Easy now, young Zeitlind. This place is safe. We can take our time talking about your sister.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Shameless fellow. Hilda called you Grandpa.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I couldn't tell you how many years ago I was born. Still, I have heard you all speak of an age long past, when the gods waged war across the land.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: In my time, there were no gods living in our lands at all. Have you ever seen an angel?

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: That makes you a great-great-great-great grandpa, Grandpa Istoria!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Nay, nay. Once you get here, all are caught within stagnant space-time. Saints and commoners, wise and foolish, young and old. There is no difference.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: That is to say, don't call me Grandpa.

dialogues.speaker: Raumhilda
dialogues.text: Then let's call each other whatever we want. I'll call you "Grandpa Istoria," and you can call me "young Hilda."

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: She was a good lass. But for some reason, she always looked a little gloomy.

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: Indeed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, stop getting sentimental! Zeitlind's suitcase has been stolen!

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Hey, give it back!

dialogues.speaker: Josephus
dialogues.text: It got away. This is going to be a difficult chase.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Wh—What do we do...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Don't let this get you down, Zeitlind. I have a theory.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, come with me.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: There it is.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Oh, thank goodness!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like we've only recovered a small part of Lind's stuff, though.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Then it's as I suspected. Your suitcase and everything inside it have been classified as relics of this age.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The rest were likely dispersed and placed in other areas.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Don't worry, Zeitlind. We'll find them together.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: ...Thank you all.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Then, shall I tell you about the themed areas?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay then, tell us.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm listening.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Besides people like us, some landscapes, relics, and even ecosystems were also uplifted to this place.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The temple was originally meant to preserve them as segments of human culture, though some gradually developed their own functions.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Take, for example, the Luyang Academy from ancient Liyue. It has now become an area devoted to art and painting.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Then there's Venipi, a laborer who once hauled stone for The Mausoleum of King Deshret. Under orders, he rebuilt a desert style complex called the Desert Pavilion.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Last is my personal favorite, the Mahavaipulya Chamber. Besides ancient texts, it also contains new novels written by some of the uplifted.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But since the purpose of the Temple of Space is preservation rather than evolution, they were also the first to face punishment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So if we go to those three places, we can find the things Zeitlind lost, right?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You could also free those areas and rescue the others. If it's not too much trouble, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh ho, Istoria. That's gonna run you extra.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: I wouldn't put it like that. We should go help everyone *and* find my things along the way.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Your personal effects are of utmost importance here, Lind. You are, after all, someone who lives in the present.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: This place is but an anthology of the past. It has no future, whereas you still have yours.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: That makes your needs the most important. Do you understand?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: In the end, a living person may amount to nothing more than a name on gravestone.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Even so, a name carries countless memories, as well as the stories and strength passed on through them, young Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Let us return and rest for now. I suspect you still have many questions.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: A cursed mountain where none who enter ever return...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um, what exactly are we looking for?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Maybe a note. A scrap of paper... Or perhaps just traces of a life that once existed here.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: With the demolition already this far along, there may not be much left to find. Still, I have to try.

dialogues.speaker: Mann
dialogues.text: And that's how it happened — I swear it on my paycheck, and the responsibilities that come with it.

dialogues.speaker: Lipphart
dialogues.text: Weren't you bemoaning how little you make as a doorman?

dialogues.speaker: Mann
dialogues.text: I'm not just any doorman. I oversee demolition work and cultural heritage preservation.

dialogues.speaker: Mann
dialogues.text: Though yeah, the pay is bad... Well, then I swear it on my reputation at the tavern.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: A most serious oath for us Mondstadters.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: I should really investigate this myself, but I still have to meet up with the Knights' expedition, who are returning to Dornman Port...

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: #Sorry about this, {NICKNAME}, but could you check out the sanatorium for me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, kinda-sorta scary stories like this usually mean something bigger's at play.

dialogues.speaker: Lipphart
dialogues.text: Then what about super scary stories?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The truth behind those is usually... Uh... basic scientific facts about how superstition can be harmful.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's fine. I know my way around a fight either way.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh, true. We've run into ghosts before, too. Most of them were actually pretty easy to talk to.

dialogues.speaker: Mann
dialogues.text: So there really are ghosts in this world?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No, no. It's all just strange elemental powers and scientific phenomena at work.

dialogues.speaker: Lipphart
dialogues.text: In that case, I won't go today. I'll just stay in Dornman Port and have some drinks.

talks.objective: Head to the sanatorium on the mountain

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. Come, come, it's team huddle time. We've a strategy meeting to hold.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Does the team include me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh, Paimon almost forgot. Istoria, do you know how to send someone back down to the ground?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I do.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then can you tell us how to send Zeitlind back? She's just an ordinary person.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: In the past, that would have been nearly impossible. But the temple's laws and order draw close unto collapse, making it now a trivial matter.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You simply need to do me a small favor.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, alright, but it better be small.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Oh, it's simple. Smash a few crappy guards, rescue an old friend, and escort us back to the center of the Pillar Hall.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound too bad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #And do you know what kind of god rules this place? {NICKNAME} is looking for her.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: This was once the sacred hall of the God of Space. But she is nowhere to be found.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: After the mistress vanished, one of the two stewards fell from grace and departed.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The one who remained, Melanta, grew increasingly severe with us. He did not descend into the mortal world, but he has descended into madness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Melanta? Does that mean that the one who fell from grace is that self-absorbed Nihilita guy?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Correct. The Watcher who introduced Dex to you is one who departed. Nihilita of Nothingness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hah, so it really was that big-winged guy who talks to himself, doesn't care what people say, and changes the subject whenever you ask him uncomfortable questions!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Huh. Does he really talk that much?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: *sigh* No matter. The two of them were once divine familiars who watched over the world from the Pillar Hall of Space.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: The Temple of Space selects people and objects from a specific historical age or a now-vanished civilization, using them as the smallest possible segments.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Once elevated, the chosen are preserved here as living memories, forever.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: That doesn't sound like a very happy fate.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I suspect it was not originally designed as an eternal paradise or some heaven in the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Still, the God of Space's sisters would occasionally bring things of interest into the temple and grant small pardons for acts of change.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it. This place was a spotless but dull bookshelf that the sisters then covered in stickers and stuffed with light novels.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Then Melanta, driven by longing for his creator, reversed all the rules to their original form. He began purging everything that had changed, punishing anyone who broke from precedent.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: I gathered the courage to leave the relative safety of the temple's center, hoping I might be able to save an old friend.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: But my lack of Pankration training caught up with me, and I ended up getting chased by the guards and hiding in that spot earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright. That's the introduction. What's our plan?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: We fight our way through and save anyone we know.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Fine. Looks like Melanta's the highest up the ladder we can reach for now. Hopefully, we can get some answers from him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's as we thought. There's nothing in the graveyard.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Old Mann must've made a mistake...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Still, look at the portrait on this grave. This girl was so young... There's a sad story behind this one for sure.
Are you friends of my sister too?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You look... exactly the same.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: S—Sister...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, so, you've gotta be the younger sister of the person buried here, right?
Well, are you also her friends?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I... don't think we count.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You scared the old man at the gate last night, so the Knights sent us to investigate.
I see. Well, I'm just here to look for her. I didn't expect that rumor to be true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A rumor?
That "those who go to the sanatorium will stay there," or something similar.
In her letters, my sister said the sanatorium was about to close, and that she was going somewhere far away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Um... M—Maybe she went traveling around the world or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No wait. Her gravestone is right here... Sorry.
It's alright. Before I came, I thought the same way you did. It took me some time to prepare myself before I could come here for answers.
I might have arrived a bit too late last night and ended up frightening the old man.
Please help me pass along my apology. I'm sorry for causing all this trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's okay. Paimon totally gets you. Just gotta explain it to everyone, and you'll be fine.
It was a little late last night. I'd planned to ask the old man about the situation, but he fled without even looking back.
For now, I want to look for traces of how she lived her life. Perhaps that would lead us to some clues on... why she would...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Y'know what? Let us help you. It's getting late, and the sooner we finish, the sooner we can head down the mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Right, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: By the way, what's your name?
Ah...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What is it? Is it an, uh, embarrassing name or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: In that case, Paimon can, uh, give you a nickname... How's that sound?
No. It's just... I had planned to... Well, I came to say goodbye.
Hmm...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Zeitlind. My name is Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Alright then. Let's help Zeitlind look around together, shall we, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's so much dust on the bed. It must've been meant for sanatorium patients back in the day, right?

talks.objective: Look for the traces left by Zeitlind's older sister
Look for the traces left by Zeitlind's older sister

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zeitlind! Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Mm. I'm fine. My sense of time's a bit off, though. Like a very long while has passed, and yet also just an instant.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That sounds like a familiar feeling.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You've felt this way before?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: You must've been through plenty of misfortune, too. How long has it been for you, then?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About... five hundred years?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: What? Has so much time passed already?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, no. {F#She's}{M#He's} talking about the time-weirdness stuff that happened to {F#her}{M#him}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That said, Paimon's not sure if "five hundred years" is that accurate at this point either.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: As for this time, it's only been about ten minutes or so?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Huh. So that's how long it's been?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Say...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Hmm?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You never asked us for our names.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Ah, yes. When I tried to call for help just now, I realized I didn't even know what to call you.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Sorry. At first, I was planning to... Well, never mind.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #I already know that you're {NICKNAME}. What about your pet?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey! Paimon's not a pet! Paimon's {NICKNAME}'s best guide and companion!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, Paimon's not a pet.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And if you're gonna make another corny joke, you can stuff it.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Oh. I'm sorry, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: #Well then. Hello, Paimon. Hello {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We'll make sure you get back down safely. But for now, we don't have any leads as to how.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So let's keep moving forward. We need to find someone and ask them what's going on.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Zeitlind, were you waiting for us here?

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: No. I think... Something feels off...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Uh... was that always so far away?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? This place looks kinda different from before.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What happened here...?)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa!

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: I am Nihilita, Watcher of Nothingness, the Open-Eyed.

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: Noble traveler from distant realms, returnee from the sea of stars... Greetings. I bid you welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: It... knows you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: But I don't know it.

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: As it should be. We dwell within the watchtowers of the world. We were never meant to meet, even across countless ages.

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: Yet I have now fallen into the mortal realm, for one purpose alone. I beg that you ascend to the high heavens and free the Aiones of the past from their inverted fates.

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: Please, touch the Anemo Archon's statue over there. It is a gateway that leads unto the heavens.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! Can't you see that there's an ordinary person here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are you sure Zeitlind is supposed to hear these things? At least let us take her back first!

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: Inconceivable. You really came...

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Ah!

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: Please remain calm. I merely placed her under my protection, so that she shall not suffer any apathic afflictions after ascending.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you mean we're bringing Zeitlind with us?

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: She has her own journey to embark upon. When you reach the temple above the sky, she will be restored.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, hold on! We never agreed to go to some strange place like that. Let Zeitlind out first!

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: This is not some strange place. It is the seat of governance above the skies. Its name is "Segment-Domain Tau." Or perhaps, let us use its lost name.

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: The Temple of Space.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Temple of Space...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (And what it just did earlier...)

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: That is correct. It belongs to the god who once appeared before you, my creator. Within the temple, you shall find your answers.

dialogues.speaker: Nihilita
dialogues.text: Please take this with you. It will aid you in my stead.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! What is this thing?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, could you explain what it actually is!?

response.speaker: Nihilita
response.text: A Watcher does not explain. A Watcher observes, in silence.

response.speaker: Nihilita
response.text: Once safety may be guaranteed, it will restore Zeitlind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't just assume that we're going! You're just looking to dump responsibility for this onto someone, aren't you?

response.speaker: Nihilita
response.text: Noble outlander, are you willing to go?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There it is again, talking to yourself and dodging the question. You haven't been making any sense for a while now, y'know?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, do you know what it's trying to say?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, sure. If that's what you want, then Paimon will go with you.

response.speaker: Nihilita
response.text: If my earlier discourtesy has stirred anger within you, come at me with blade in hand. I will await you in the mortal world.

choices.text: A little strange, but kind of cute.

dialogues.text: Some people just won't listen. I already told you, now's not the time to go up the mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Easy there, Old Mann. Let's calm down and talk this out.
We were getting along just fine earlier at the Night Brew.
But the moment I mentioned I was heading for Windrest Peak, he grabbed me and dragged me all the way here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Huffman. What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: As you can see, Old Mann is trying his best to keep people away from Windrest Peak.

dialogues.speaker: Huffman
dialogues.text: Anyway, let me introduce you. This is Lipphart, an adventurer.

dialogues.speaker: Mann
dialogues.text: What I saw... What I felt... It was terrifying! Surely you don't wish to hear it?

dialogues.speaker: Lipphart
dialogues.text: Doesn't look like I'm going anywhere today, so let's hear it. Consider it an extension of our drinking and bragging session from earlier.

dialogues.speaker: Lipphart
dialogues.text: So, what sort of "great peril" are we facing here?

dialogues.speaker: Mann
dialogues.text: The sanatorium's haunted! Seriously! I saw them ghosts with my own eyes!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ghosts!?

dialogues.speaker: Mann
dialogues.text: It happened last night...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello!
Huh!? Humans...? I thought the "uplifting" had already ended. More cases like Hilda's, then?
No, wait. Perhaps you were simply unlucky. Newcomers who have only recently passed the trial of the Apathic Interval, maybe?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Greetings, newcomers. My name is Istoria. I hail from the age when the Dark Dragon King rent the sky open. And you are?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What sorta age was that?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: #Anyway, call me {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Zeitlind
dialogues.text: Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Hmm. So, you're Zeitlind.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Ah. Dexter. You are here as well!

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Now I understand. You must be people of the present age. In which case, you have come to reinforce us!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was quick!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, Dex's real name is Dexter, huh? Is it your friend?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: No. We call it Dex too. But it just sent me a secret signal.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: As such, I introduced it using the more official, more impressive-sounding name.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hey, Hey, {NICKNAME}. Paimon wants a formal name and a secret code, too.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Ah, but now is not the time for such talk.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Since Nihilita has sent you up here, that means it is finally our time to strike back.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute! We're still confused.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: How confused? More confused than I was the first time I looked upon Escher's paintings?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: E...scher? As in, Escher the Engineer?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Does the name ring a bell? He's from a very long time ago, though. Surely not someone you know...

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Eh, you know what? Who knows. Maybe he really was famous. Actually, that pisses me off. Why didn't I make my mark in history?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: You know what? Let's just call him "Maukie" from now on.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Escher?

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: Just an unlucky, ill-natured painter.

dialogues.speaker: Istoria
dialogues.text: His family calls him "Maukie", and so do we.
